paper.title_en: Left-right symmetry breaking in $E_6^L\times E_6^R$ occurs only in spacetime -- with possible implications for strong $CP$
paper.abstract_en: Two-sided octonionic $E_6^L\times E_6^R$ unification trinifies each factor and so carries two colour groups: the visible $SU(3)_c$ and a second $SU(3)_{c'}$ which, gauged like the first, would colour the charged lepton and must be suppressed by hand. We argue no such device is needed: the left-right symmetry acts in spacetime, not internally -- in the gravi-weak reading $SU(2)_R$ is the gravitational frame group and the exchange is ordinary parity on the Dirac field; a spacetime operation cannot double the internal colour. Colour is single and vector-like, $SU(3)_{c'}=SU(3)_c$, and the electron is a colour singlet. The right sector contributes one colour-blind datum, $\sqrt m$ (values: the exceptional-Jordan trace split, an input; $N_R$ fixes only the colour representation). An anomaly no-go shows that no gauged $U(1)$ on the visible fermions can carry the $\sqrt m$ pattern: the dark-electromagnetic $U(1)_{\rm dem}$ carries the parity mirror of electric charge on the dark sector, the visible fermions are dem-neutral, and no visible fifth force is predicted. Hypercharge is recovered as the consistency relation $Y=Q-T^3_L$, $Q=N/3$. As an application, parity restricts the QCD angle to $\{0,π\}$; $θ_{\rm QCD}=0$ is selected, not derived, by matching to the sign content of the quark mass determinant, whose phase vanishes because the flavour rotors have real determinant. Hence $\barθ=0$ at tree level, conditional on the gravi-weak identification, with a nonzero CKM phase. Loop stability is open: the two-loop $\barθ$ of the minimal universal-seesaw parity model arises from scalar exchange, so the absence of a gauged $W_R$ here does not remove its mechanism, which the Higgs-bridge sector shares. We tag throughout what is derived, what is input, and what is open.
